name: Dubbo
note: Drive order is east to west through the CBD, a guess because the approach road is not known. Coordinates are from Wikipedia, cross-checked against OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) on 2026-10-20 where a match existed. Banks stop combines two buildings 22 m apart; Milestone stop combines Talbragar Chambers 45 m away. Old Dubbo Gaol hangings deliberately left out (family friendly). Extras are manual stories.

intro.name: Welcome
intro.text: Welcome to Dubbo, called Dhubu in the Wiradjuri language. Wiradjuri people have lived in this area for over 40,000 years. The explorer John Oxley was the first European to report on it, in 1818, and the Dulhunty family settled on a property here in the early 1830s. Dubbo became a city in 1966, and it sits where the Newell, Mitchell and Golden highways meet.

stops.name: Railway station
stops.coordCheckedOsm: OSM -32.2456365, 148.6082178, 152 m apart. FLAG: over 100 m, may fire early or late. Wikipedia point kept.
stops.text: Dubbo railway station opened on 1 February 1881. It was built of stone, to a design from the office of John Whitton, the NSW engineer in chief. Dubbo was a big junction, where the Main Western line met lines to Molong and Coonamble, and its locomotive depot was the limit for the heavier steam engines. The stone platform faces are rare, and the station has been heritage listed since 1999.

stops.name: Old Dubbo Gaol
stops.text: Behind the high red brown brick wall at 90 Macquarie Street is the Old Dubbo Gaol, with a watchtower on its corner. It replaced earlier lock-ups from 1847 and 1862, and closed as a gaol in 1966. Plans to knock it down for an office block were dropped after local protests, and it reopened as a tourist attraction in 1974.

stops.name: Macquarie Street banks
stops.coordCheckedOsm: Wikipedia points -32.2467,148.6017 (CML) and -32.2466,148.6019 (NAB), 22 m apart so combined at midpoint. Not checked against OSM.
stops.text: Look for two grand bank buildings on Macquarie Street. The Colonial Mutual Life building at number 118 opened on 23 February 1885 as the Australian Joint Stock Bank, and it won a place on the State Heritage Register in 1999 after a community campaign. Close by, at 110 to 114, is the former Commercial Banking Company building, built around 1906 and 1907 to a design by Laurie and Heath.
stops.navName: Colonial Mutual Life building, 118 Macquarie Street

stops.name: Milestone Hotel and old bank
stops.coordCheckedOsm: Milestone OSM 5 m from Wikipedia point. Combined at midpoint with Talbragar Shire Council Chambers (Wikipedia -32.2508,148.6003, 45 m apart).
stops.text: Two heritage buildings stand close together here. The Milestone Hotel, on the corner of Macquarie and Bultje Streets, was built in 1882 in the Victorian Italianate style. Nearby are the Talbragar Shire Council Chambers, built in 1867 as the first bank in Dubbo. That bank was the town's only one until 1876. Both are on the State Heritage Register.

stops.name: L.H. Ford Bridge
stops.coordCheckedOsm: OSM -32.2514808, 148.5968325, 115 m apart. FLAG: long bridge, point likely differs by end
stops.text: The L.H. Ford Bridge carries the Mitchell Highway over the Macquarie River, which the Wiradjuri call Wambuul. It opened on 26 September 1969 and is named after Les Ford, a former mayor of Dubbo. At 613 metres it was the fourth longest highway bridge in New South Wales when it was finished, and it replaced an old wooden bridge.

extras.name: Taronga Western Plains Zoo
extras.coordCheckedOsm: OSM -32.2820266, 148.579882, 1321 m apart. FLAG: large site, OSM point probably the entrance or centre. Manual only so no effect on triggers.
extras.text: Taronga Western Plains Zoo, about 5 kilometres from the city, opened on 28 February 1977. It spreads across 300 hectares of woodland and grassland, and hidden moats stand in for fences so the animals seem to share the space with you. It opened with 35 different animals from six countries. A great pick for a nearly five year old.

extras.name: Dundullimal Homestead
extras.coordCheckedOsm: OSM -32.2857393, 148.6033923, 152 m apart. FLAG: over 100 m. Manual only.
extras.text: Dundullimal Homestead, about 7 kilometres south of Dubbo on the Macquarie River, was built around 1842 by John Maughan. It is believed to be the oldest surviving slab hut house in Australia, and the National Trust looks after it. It began as a sheep station, in a district where squatters ran their stock well beyond the official limits of settlement.

extras.name: Western Plains Cultural Centre
extras.text: The Western Plains Cultural Centre sits beside Victoria Park. It opened on 10 February 2007 and holds a gallery, a museum and a community arts centre. The museum is in the old Dubbo High School hall from 1917. Look out for the wool wagon, described as Australia's largest and best preserved.

extras.name: Royal Flying Doctor Service
extras.text: The Royal Flying Doctor Service base at Dubbo Airport has a visitor centre that opened in 2019. You can see a King Air 200 aircraft up close and try interactive displays about how doctors reach people in the outback. A great pick for a nearly five year old.

extras.name: Macquarie River railway bridge
extras.text: The Macquarie River railway bridge was finished in 1884. It is a wrought iron lattice bridge with three continuous spans, the longest 48 metres. It was load tested on 23 April 1884 and went into service the next month.
